think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 42-year-old immunosuppressed man from the endemic Jizan region of Saudi Arabia on prednisone and mycophenolate presents with profound fevers, pancytopenia, hyperferritinemia, and hepatosplenomegaly after consuming raw goat milk and swimming in freshwater valleys. The clinical constellation triggers a broad differential including zoonotic infections (brucellosis, malaria, Q fever), systemic lupus flare/autoimmune disease, and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Furthermore, initial bone marrow examination failed to detect classic Leishman-Donovan bodies, creating a diagnostic pitfall.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Concludes after emergency triage examination, baseline hematologic/metabolic laboratory testing, and abdominal ultrasound demonstrating hepatosplenomegaly, strictly before send-out viral/zoonotic/autoimmune serologic panels, bone marrow aspiration, liver biopsy, and anti-Leishmania ELISA.
3. Differential Distinctions: Brucellosis is strongly suggested by exposure to goats/sheep and consumption of unpasteurized goat milk in the Arabian Peninsula, but excluded by negative Brucella serology and sterile bone marrow cultures. Malaria is suggested by fevers, rigors, anemia, and splenomegaly, but excluded by repeated negative peripheral blood thick and thin smears. Autoimmune glomerulonephritis flare / systemic lupus erythematosus is excluded by negative ANA, ANCA, anti-GBM, and cryoglobulins. Visceral leishmaniasis is confirmed by liver biopsy showing granulomatous hepatitis with extramedullary hematopoiesis, positive anti-Leishmania ELISA, and prompt response to liposomal amphotericin B.
case_prompt:
A 42-year-old Saudi male residing in the Jizan province presents with a 3-week history of daily intermittent fevers accompanied by nocturnal shaking chills and rigors that fail to respond to antipyretics. He also reports diffuse colicky abdominal pain, nausea, non-bloody vomiting occurring 2–3 times daily, profound fatigue, anorexia, and an unintentional 7-kg weight loss. His past medical history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and histologically-proven chronic glomerulonephritis diagnosed three months earlier, for which he is actively maintained on daily immunosuppressive therapy with mycophenolate mofetil (1 g twice daily) and oral prednisone (20 mg once daily). Epidemiological history reveals frequent contact with goats and sheep, ingestion of raw unpasteurized goat milk, and recreational swimming in local valley freshwater bodies. He denies cough, hemoptysis, diarrhea, dysuria, skin rash, oral ulcers, arthralgia, or contact with individuals with chronic respiratory disease.

On physical examination, he is obese, pale, and diaphoresis is noted without jaundice or cyanosis. Vital signs reveal a body temperature of 38.6°C, pulse rate of 98 beats/min, respiratory rate of 24 breaths/min, blood pressure of 125/85 mmHg, and oxygen saturation of 100% on ambient air. Head and neck examination reveals normal jugular venous pressure and absence of mucosal lesions. Abdominal examination demonstrates mild epigastric tenderness, a palpably enlarged liver extending 4 cm below the right costal margin with an estimated total span of 15 cm, and fullness in the left upper quadrant.

Initial laboratory investigations reveal marked pancytopenia: white blood cell count 2,650/µL (neutrophils 72.1%, lymphocytes 23.2%, monocytes 4%, eosinophils 0.7%), hemoglobin 8.8 g/dL, and platelet count 87,000/µL, with a reticulocyte count of 1.28%. The erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) is 88 mm/hr, serum ferritin is markedly elevated at 1,000 ng/mL, and transferrin saturation is 11.2%. Serum chemistries demonstrate sodium 138 mEq/L, potassium 3.2 mEq/L, bicarbonate 25 mmol/L, blood urea nitrogen 12 mg/dL, and serum creatinine 2.15 mg/dL. Liver biochemical tests show total protein 6.1 g/dL, albumin 3.2 g/dL, total bilirubin 1.2 mg/dL, alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 71 IU/L, aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 42 IU/L, alkaline phosphatase 179 IU/L, and gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) 447 IU/L. Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) is elevated at 732 U/L, and C-reactive protein (CRP) is 53 mg/L. Urinalysis demonstrates microscopic hematuria (10–25 RBCs/hpf) and 2–5 WBCs/hpf without nitrites. Direct and indirect Coombs tests and sickling tests are negative. Plain chest radiograph and electrocardiogram are normal. Abdominal ultrasonography confirms hepatomegaly with a 16.2-cm liver span and splenomegaly measuring 14.0 cm in bipolar diameter, with increased renal cortical echogenicity and no ascites.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Given the patient's direct contact with goats and sheep, consumption of unpasteurized goat milk, and presentation with undulating fevers and hepatosplenomegaly in Saudi Arabia, brucellosis was strongly suspected; however, specific Brucella serologic testing and bone marrow cultures were negative.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The serological tests for... Brucella were negative... Bone marrow culture for Brucella was negative.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Endemic vector exposure, nocturnal fevers, chills, hemolytic anemia, and splenomegaly suggested plasmodial infection, but repeated peripheral blood smears and blood cultures were negative.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Malaria smear and blood cultures were also negative.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Systemic autoimmune flare / Lupus nephritis with secondary HLH
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Pre-existing glomerulonephritis, cytopenias, and high ferritin raised concern for an autoimmune flare or systemic vasculitis, but comprehensive autoimmune serologies including ANA, ANCA, anti-GBM, anti-SSA/SSB, and cryoglobulins were negative.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Rheumatoid factor, antinuclear antibody, antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody, antiglomerular basement membrane antibody, anti-Sjogren's syndrome A and B antibodies and cryoglobulin were negative.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: In an immunosuppressed patient from the Jizan endemic focus with progressive pancytopenia and splenomegaly, diagnostic bone marrow smear was falsely negative for amastigotes, but liver biopsy demonstrated granulomatous hepatitis with extramedullary hematopoiesis, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) confirmed anti-Leishmania antibodies, and targeted liposomal amphotericin B resulted in complete clinical recovery.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Liver biopsy showed granulomatous hepatitis with extramedullary hematopoiesis... Additional serological testing using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) releveled the presence of anti-Leishmania antibodies. Based on this, the patient was started on liposomal amphotericin B course as a treatment for VL... After 1 week, the patient improved clinically, the fever subsided, the laboratory parameters began to improve and at the end of liposomal amphotericin B course, all tests returned to normal.

editor_comments: High-fidelity distillation capturing visceral leishmaniasis occurring under pharmacologic immunosuppression in an endemic Saudi Arabian province, complicated by negative bone marrow smears and multiple zoonotic exposures. Fully adheres to admission breakpoint.
